sourceInformation.genre: Open-world first-person shooter with survival pressure and systemic fire
sourceInformation.perspective: First person on foot, at the wheel and in story scenes, with an optional chase camera in vehicles
sourceInformation.tech: Pixel Engine (riftlight) 0.46.0, three.js r186, Rapier 0.20, esbuild 0.28.2, Playwright 1.63.0 for tests; game code in plain JavaScript modules
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine native 3D-as-pixel-art look at 480x270, toon materials, 16-colour palette; new models written as data for people, guns, vehicles and buildings; sand, orange and red land with plum shadows
sourceInformation.animation: Engine ClipDef data compiled to AnimationMixer clips on the hero rig, lower/upper body layering, Ragdoll on death; first-person hands and guns keyed by data clips
sourceInformation.audio: All sound written in code: SoundDef effects, Song music (default volume 10 percent), and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared-world mode, 1 to 4 players (Cash Run); also solo with hired guns and a same-computer link
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node suites (static, systems, playthrough, replay) plus Playwright Chromium on file:// and the AI Hub harness scenarios; no review subagents
sourceInformation.research: The plan supplied with the brief, the engine kit GUIDE/ASSETS/API docs and the AI Hub protocol README; no other research

testingFeedback: 15 logged in tests/ISSUES.md, plus a few small ones fixed on the spot.

The scripted playthrough: a bot plays M0 to both endings through the real key, mouse and hold-to-use input, with different choices in two runs. It exposed the frozen AI positions, the Rapier panic and the broken mission wiring that no unit test saw.
The attract-mode run: it proves the tour loops without errors but cannot say whether any beat looks right; only screenshots can, and software rendering shows about one frame a second.
engineFeedback: Engine.headless with step(): fast, repeatable play in Node, and models, textures and sounds as plain data that a sheets tool and renderSound can check without a display. The pixel pipeline makes everything look like one game at once.

Yes: Node read pixel-engine.js as CommonJS until package.json said type module; CharacterController.feet returns a fresh vector, not a live one, so my AI froze; removing a controller body with physics.remove panics Rapier; the headless camera is not first person unless asked.

Everything that makes it a game: the 5 m fire grid and its look, first-person hands and wear and jams, soldier AI, the mission and dialogue runner, the screen and prompt system, and the Cash Run netcode.
First person and menus: replacing the rig step, owning pointer lock, a HUD with only a 5x7 font, and judging a 3D scene at one frame a second without being able to watch it move.
Give CharacterController a documented dispose and a live feet vector, so characters can be retired and read safely.
promptFeedback: The plan decided what to build and listed verified engine traps, so effort went into building; the cut order and the done list kept scope honest.

How much a single run can finish: the plan is a whole game plus multiplayer, attract mode and dev mode, and some rules pull against each other, such as six items a screen against twenty balance sliders.
Breadth: keeping nine systems consistent while every check ran headless, and proving the story could be finished by a bot.
Name a minimum bar and a budget, and say which cuts are acceptable up front; split the plan into milestones with their own done lists.

aiHub.name: Far Pry 2
aiHub.description: An original first-person war-zone survival shooter: guns that rust and jam, a fever on a timetable, grass fires that follow the wind, three friends for hire and a map that turns out to be the plot. Includes the Cash Run shared-world mode for 1 to 4 players.
aiHub.controls: Pad: sticks move and look, R2 fire, L2 aim, Square use or reload, L1 heal, D-pad up map. Keyboard and mouse: WASD, mouse, LMB fire, RMB aim, E use, R reload, Q heal, M map.
